state:
Goal `core-objectset`: six of `Core\ObjectSet`'s nine members have all their feature proofs —
`add`, `has`, `remove`, `count`, `isEmpty` and `clear`. The class card is in
`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/objset.rs`'s `CARD`. What still owes is the algebra: `union`, `intersect` and
`diff` owe about, examples, hostile, perf and a test from each side. The Rust test
`clear_empties_a_set_that_add_can_fill_again` now also covers `isEmpty`.
Reading `identity_store::vacate` found a reorder under a hash collision. It is recorded as
`data/gaps/nvs-stdlib/a-removal-inside-a-hash-chain-reorders-the-collection.json` (M12), and the
`remove` about page does not promise the order after a removal. No proof failed.
A member bench must not index an array in its loop: `$keys[$total % 3]` costs 2 allocations per
round, so the three new benches pick with a ternary between two variables.

backlog: The chain reorder on removal is a gap record, `data/gaps/nvs-stdlib/a-removal-inside-a-hash-chain-reorders-the-collection.json`, owned by M12; a Rust test planting a collision can pin it when it is fixed.

The `remove` bench does 1 allocation of 50 bytes a round. It belongs to the `add` that re-inserts, the same owned-key copy as `data/gaps/nvs-stdlib/an-objectmap-overwrite-allocates-its-chain-key.json`.
